Documentation → Releases → 2.10.0

SATOM 2.10.0

Job notices can be minimised, the deep capture shows real progress, and Device health is filled in right after a rediscovery.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Minimise job notices
  • Fixed
  • Deep capture sat at "running…" at 100 % with no count
  • Device health said "never harvested" right after a rediscovery
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-10-03 · All releases

In short#

This release answers three requests from people using SATOM every day. Job notices can now be folded down to a single line, the deep capture of a rediscovery shows what it is doing instead of sitting at 100 %, and Device health no longer claims a device was "never harvested" just after you rediscovered it.

What's new#

Minimise job notices#

Each notice in the jobs dock (the stack of job toasts on screen) now has a − button.

  • A minimised notice is one line: the job title, its percent and a thin progress bar.
  • Click □ or the title to bring it back to full size, with its message and its Stop button.
  • Your choice is remembered when you move to another page or reload, for the rest of the browser session.
  • Dismissing a notice forgets the choice.

This keeps long-running jobs visible without covering the page you are working on.

Fixed#

Deep capture sat at "running…" at 100 % with no count#

With Capture full WPP + policy depth turned on, the rediscovery bar reached 100 % and then showed only "Deep capture (WPP + policy graph) running…" for as long as the deep pass took. Now:

  • The deep pass first lists the server policies and web protection profiles it will read, then reports each one as it starts.
  • The bar switches to the deep pass's own percent, and the line reads, for example, Deep capture 5/23 · 8 server policies, 14 WPPs · WPP 3/12 followed by the profile name.
  • The job notice in the dock and the Jobs page show the same line and percent.
  • The finished summary says how many server policies and profiles the depth came from.
  • A long deep pass no longer looks like a job that has died: each object it reads counts as a sign of life.

Device health said "never harvested" right after a rediscovery#

After a rediscovery, Device health could show no cached configuration on this node, never harvested and 4 probes have never run. Two things changed:

  • A rediscovery now fills the local cache. Until now only the hourly harvest updated the cache that Device health, the section pages and the inventory read. A successful rediscovery now does it too, and it is recorded as a harvest run started by a rediscovery. A rediscovery and an hourly harvest of the same configuration count as one version, not two. If the cache cannot be updated, the rediscovery still finishes as done and its summary says local cache not updated with the reason.
  • Device health explains a missing schedule. A fresh installation does not schedule the hourly harvest or the deep monitor sweep on its own; they are added when an administrator seeds the default scheduled actions. When Harvest, Cache or Deep monitors has nothing to show and no schedule covers the device, the reason now says that no such schedule exists on this node and gives the command to create the default schedules.

The no hardware inventory note now points you to the Scan hardware (SSH) button: a rediscovery, even with its SSH CLI capture, does not collect hardware details.
